root_idea.summary: The root centers on aversion joined with fault, blame, or disparagement.
root_idea.development: This orientation develops into blaming or finding fault, despising and abasing, and associated expulsion; Form IV extends the range to frightening or compelling someone against his will.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested passive participle is displayed under the normalized singular citation form مَذْءُوم.

senses.definition: One who is blamed, reproached, or held at fault.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic passive-participle use in the occurrence at 7:18; it emphasizes the person's blameworthiness or disgrace. The corresponding Form I lexical branch includes blaming and finding fault.

senses.definition: One who is driven away or banished.
senses.usage_conditions: An alternative interpretation of the same Quranic passive participle at 7:18, emphasizing expulsion rather than blame.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To despise or scorn; to abase or humiliate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb. Reported combined uses include despising while blaming, driving the object away, or beating the object.
A distinct Form I verbal use equivalent to repaying or requiting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compel someone, against his will, to do something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV construction used with عَلَى to express compelled action against the person's will.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vice, fault, defect, or similar blemish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Substantive noun for a fault or defect; the form is also recorded as the verbal noun of ذَأَمَ.
Attested in the idiom مَا سَمِعْتُ لَهُ ذَأْمَةً, meaning that no word was heard from him.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Blame, contempt or abasement with reported expulsion and beating variants, and requital are represented.
The Form IV frightening or terrifying use is represented.
The against-the-will compulsion construction is represented.
The noun meaning fault or defect is represented.
The idiomatic noun meaning word or utterance is represented.
The Quran-attested interpretations blamed, driven away, and banished are represented by two senses.

cautions: Lane's printed Quran citation for this form appears as historical '[vii. 17]' and is not converted into a modern verse location; the supplied QAC occurrence and Quran-focused evidence securely identify the occurrence as 7:18.
